name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,787

entries.clue: Badmouth country gent on a regular basis (6)

indicatorNotes.on a regular basis: taking letters at regular intervals: every other letter of 'gent'

blocks.note: G and N, the first and third letters of GENT

annotation.surface: A country gentleman is routinely slandered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country gent' reads as one person, a squire, but the setter splits it: 'country' is a separate piece and only 'gent' is thinned out.
annotation.definitionFit: To malign someone is to speak ill of them, which is what badmouthing means.

entries.clue: Implied temperature is below average (5)

indicatorNotes.is below: in a down clue, T sits below MEAN in the grid

blocks.note: T = temperature, as in physics formulas

annotation.surface: A weather report hinting that the temperature is lower than usual.
annotation.walkthrough: The order is reversed from the clue: 'temperature' comes first in the words but last in the answer because it is placed below.
annotation.definitionFit: What you meant is what you implied, both past tenses of intending a sense.

entries.clue: Unadorned parts of wall are tiled over (7)

indicatorNotes.parts of: the answer is made of parts of the following words
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, 'over' means turned upside down, so read backwards

blocks.note: waLL ARE TILed, the run of letters spanning the three words

annotation.surface: A plain wall has been covered with tiles.
annotation.walkthrough: The irony is that tiling a wall adorns it; the definition fits a literal translation, one without embellishment.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal account is plain and unembellished, sticking to the bare words.

entries.clue: Two-tone classic brown robe for Spooner (5,4)

indicatorNotes.for Spooner: the Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of two words, so the two things clued here trade their fronts

blocks.note: to brown bread is to toast it; that word gives up its T and takes the G sound
a gown is a robe; it hands over its G and takes the T

annotation.surface: A classic garment in two shades of brown.
annotation.walkthrough: 2 Tone was a British ska label of the late 1970s; 'Ghost Town' by The Specials, its best-known band, went to number one in 1981. 'Two-tone' pretends to describe a colour scheme.
annotation.definitionFit: Ghost Town is the signature hit of the 2 Tone ska movement, so a classic of that genre.

entries.clue: Wretched sailor given hollow justice by court (6)

indicatorNotes.hollow: a hollow word has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters
indicatorNotes.by: beside: the pieces are set next to each other

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court

annotation.surface: A miserable sailor gets only a sham of justice from a court martial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Given' just joins the sailor to what follows; 'hollow justice' sounds like a verdict on the trial but is an instruction to empty the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Abject means miserable and wretched, as in abject poverty.

entries.clue: Judge sequesters large Dickensian house? (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is by example: BLEAK is the word that goes with 'House' in the title of Dickens's novel Bleak House

indicatorNotes.sequesters: to sequester is to shut away, so BEAK encloses L

blocks.note: beak is British slang for a magistrate or judge
L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A judge isolating a jury in a large house, perhaps one from Dickens.
annotation.walkthrough: Bleak House is Dickens's novel about an endless court case, so the judge in the surface is fitting. The question mark flags that the answer only completes the title.
annotation.definitionFit: Bleak House is a Dickens novel, so BLEAK is the Dickensian word for that house.

entries.clue: Chained wild animal (7)

indicatorNotes.wild: wild letters run out of control into a new order

annotation.surface: A wild beast kept on a chain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wild animal' reads as one phrase; 'wild' has to be peeled off as the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.

entries.clue: Very sensitive street cop is rattled (3-6)

indicatorNotes.is rattled: rattled letters are shaken into a new order

annotation.surface: A touchy police officer on the beat is shaken up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very sensitive' seems to describe the cop's temperament; it is the classification of a document.
annotation.definitionFit: Top-secret information is the most sensitive grade of classified material.

entries.clue: Throw a wobbly meeting German swine (7)

indicatorNotes.wobbly: wobbly letters are unsteady and fall into a new order
indicatorNotes.meeting: joining up with: G is placed next to the anagram

blocks.note: the letters of THROW A rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone throws a tantrum on meeting a German brute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Throw a wobbly' is British slang for having a tantrum, and it reads as one idiom; the setter splits it into fodder and instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The warthog is a wild African pig, so a swine.

entries.clue: American criminals smuggling heroin back from Alaska, possibly (7)

indicatorNotes.smuggling: the criminals carry something hidden inside them
indicatorNotes.back from: the back of Alaska, its last letter

blocks.note: perps is American slang for perpetrators

annotation.surface: US gangsters bringing heroin in from Alaska, maybe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a reversal instruction, but it points to the end of Alaska, not a word read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Perhaps and possibly both mark something as uncertain.

entries.clue: Most picturesque island crossed by soldier partaking in mission (9)

indicatorNotes.crossed by: the soldier runs across the island, so the soldier goes around I
indicatorNotes.partaking in: taking part inside: the soldier and island together go into the mission

annotation.surface: A soldier on a mission crosses the prettiest island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' is the crossword's favourite insect, not a human in uniform, and 'crossed by' makes the island the thing enclosed.
annotation.definitionFit: Quaint means attractively old-fashioned, so the quaintest is the most picturesque.

entries.clue: Impressed by celebrity side's lead in opening phase of rugby match (10)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the side's first letter inside the word for opening, splitting it after its fourth letter

blocks.note: a ruck is a phase of play in rugby, players contesting a ball on the ground

annotation.surface: Something about the opening of a rugby game and the side leading it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Celebrity' looks like the source of the answer's first half, but it belongs to the definition; the surface's rugby match hides a word for beginning broken open.
annotation.definitionFit: To be starstruck is to be dazzled by a famous person.

entries.clue: Food and drink conference (4)

blocks.note: what someone habitually eats and drinks
a formal assembly or parliament; the historic one at Worms condemned Luther

annotation.surface: A catering item for a meeting.
annotation.walkthrough: The Diet of Worms was the 1521 imperial assembly that condemned Luther; Japan's parliament is still called by the same name.
annotation.definitionFit: The word means both the food and drink a person takes and a legislative assembly.

entries.clue: Hail of projectiles from colossal volcano (5)

indicatorNotes.from: the answer is taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: coloSSAL VOlcano, spanning the two words

annotation.surface: Rocks raining down from an erupting volcano.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is volcanic, so 'hail of projectiles' reads as flying rock rather than gunfire.
annotation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns or missiles.

entries.clue: Ogre rings Independent in middle of night, screaming (9)

indicatorNotes.rings: SHREK forms a ring around I

blocks.note: Shrek, the ogre of the animated films
I = Independent, the paper this puzzle appeared in

annotation.surface: A monster circles the newspaper office at midnight, yelling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction but is just the letters IN.
annotation.definitionFit: Shrieking is screaming in a high, piercing voice.

entries.clue: Setter does note attempt to show great reverence (8)

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as I
the same verb in its base form, as in 'I do'
la, the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: The crossword setter makes a stab at showing deep respect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Setter does' reads as a statement about the compiler, but setter and verb are two separate pieces, and the verb loses its third-person ending.
annotation.definitionFit: Idolatry is worship of an idol, or extreme admiration.

entries.clue: Pretentious maiden, say, hit on knight (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the pieces sit on top of one another

blocks.note: a maiden is an over in cricket with no runs scored; 'say' marks it as one example

annotation.surface: A young woman strikes a knight, like a scene from a pompous romance.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls from one bowler; a maiden over is one where the batting side scores nothing. The surface's maiden is a girl.
annotation.definitionFit: Overblown writing or style is inflated and pretentious.

entries.clue: Tinder craftily engages female model as trap (5,3)

indicatorNotes.craftily: done with cunning, so the letters are reworked
indicatorNotes.engages: the rearranged letters take F and T inside them

blocks.note: the Model T, the Ford car

annotation.surface: A cunning dating-app user reels in a female model as bait.
annotation.walkthrough: Tinder is a dating app, which is why the surface is about luring a model; the capital hides the plain word for kindling that is actually rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A drift net is a large fishing net left to drift and catch fish, so a trap.

entries.clue: Fellow in his dotage raised cats (7)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: someone in his dotage is senile

annotation.surface: An old man in his decline kept cats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised cats' reads as keeping pets, but 'raised' works on SENILE.
annotation.definitionFit: Felines are members of the cat family.

entries.clue: Demand former partner do something (5)

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
to act is to do something

annotation.surface: Insisting that your ex should take action.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Demand' is a verb here, as in demanding payment, not a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: you insist on a promise or a fee and so obtain it.

entries.clue: Greed is a moral weakness consuming upstanding artist (7)

indicatorNotes.consuming: the weakness eats the artist, taking him inside
indicatorNotes.upstanding: in a down clue, standing up means reading upwards, so RA reverses

blocks.note: a vice is a moral failing

annotation.surface: A moralist's line: greed is a failing that devours even a respectable painter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' pretends to praise the artist's honesty; here it only turns him upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Latin avarus, greedy; it is the traditional name for one of the seven deadly sins.

entries.clue: Central characters in Bizet opera share violent passion (4)

indicatorNotes.Central characters in: take the middle letter of each following word

annotation.surface: The leading roles in a Bizet opera, Carmen say, are gripped by a violent passion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Central characters' suggests the leads of the opera; it means the middle letters of the four words. 'Violent' belongs to the wordplay, leaving 'passion' alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Zeal is fervent enthusiasm, a passion for something.

entries.clue: Instruments quiet, cold-blooded type installed in hospital departments (10)

indicatorNotes.installed in: SH and BOA are put inside WARDS

blocks.note: a boa is a snake, a cold-blooded reptile

annotation.surface: Hushed instruments and a heartless person have been placed in hospital wards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cold-blooded type' looks like a callous person, but it is a reptile.
annotation.definitionFit: A washboard, scraped with thimbles, is a percussion instrument in skiffle and jug bands.

entries.clue: Used to be extremely talkative? Rubbish! (5)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the extremes, the first and last letters, of 'talkative'

annotation.surface: Someone was once a great chatterer, and a listener dismisses it as nonsense.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely talkative' reads as very chatty; 'extremely' asks for the ends of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Waste is rubbish, material thrown away.

entries.clue: Picked up bunny girl's cash (5)

indicatorNotes.Picked up: picked up by the ear, heard

blocks.note: a doe is a female rabbit

annotation.surface: Someone collected a Playboy bunny's earnings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bunny girl' calls up a Playboy hostess, but it is a female rabbit. The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang synonym, like bread: both staples stand in for money.

entries.clue: See simple-minded Nationalist ousting Liberal (7)

indicatorNotes.ousting: N pushes L out and takes its place

annotation.surface: Look at the dim nationalist who has unseated the Liberal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is election-night politics; the parties are only letters swapped inside the word for stupid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to be present and watch something happen.

entries.clue: Relative presses old investigators about scrap (7)

indicatorNotes.presses: MUM squeezes the others between her letters
indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so CID reads backwards

blocks.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

annotation.surface: A family member leans on veteran detectives over a small matter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' could be a fight, which fits the surface; it is a small amount.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Latin modicus, moderate: a small amount, as a scrap is.

entries.clue: Leave detailed incantation in sacred text (6)

indicatorNotes.detailed: de-tailed: SPELL loses its tail, its last letter

annotation.surface: Leave out an elaborate magic formula from a holy book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as elaborate; split it as de-tailed, with its tail removed.
annotation.definitionFit: A gospel is one of the four books of the New Testament, a sacred text.

entries.clue: Involve Norway in carbon-free recycling scheme (6)

indicatorNotes.in: N goes into the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.recycling: recycled letters are reprocessed into a new order

blocks.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway
C is the chemical symbol for carbon, removed
SCHEME without its C, then rearranged around N

annotation.surface: Bringing Norway into a green recycling programme.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is environmental policy, and 'carbon-free' sounds like a green slogan; it only drops C from SCHEME.
annotation.definitionFit: To enmesh is to entangle or involve someone in something.
